neighbours.label: a word that picks out an open set of people ('anyone who', 'those who', 'few readers', 'not all'); relative clauses on things or named individuals stay low
fire: Honestly, anyone who has run a marathon knows that wall.
In the end, those who saved early retired more comfortably.
Sadly, few visitors ever climb all the way to the tower.
The coach thanked everyone who stayed to clean the gym.
In this town, those who fish at dawn catch the most trout.
As the guide warned, not all hikers reach the summit.
The prize goes to whoever answers first, says the host.
The doctor said anyone who feels dizzy should sit down.
quiet: Honestly, the marathon route has a steep hill near the end.
In the end, the money saved early grew more comfortably.
Sadly, the tower is closed to the public on Sundays.
The coach thanked the janitor, Mr Lee, for cleaning the gym.
In this town, the river which runs past the mill has trout.
As the guide warned, the summit trail is icy in winter.
The prize is a voucher that the host keeps in an envelope.
The doctor said the medicine which causes dizziness is gone.

short: open set of people (those who / anyone)
notes: Card peaks ' who' x12, Who x5, everyone, few, all. Probe: 'Anyone who' 0.399, 'Who knows' 0.396, 'Those who' 0.346, 'Few readers' 0.333, 'Not all' 0.256, 'Anyone with' 0.255, 'people that' 0.207; 'book which I lent' 0.038.
